title: Surface feeding and clump counts set the CPV radius law in a sparse aligned dipole model
abstract: We derive a CPV detection law for a rigid aligned dipole with uniform surface feeding, Poisson clumps and one viewing angle per star. In the sparse limit, a requirement for at least m visible clumps gives a rate proportional to x^(-(m+1)), where x is the corotation-to-stellar radius ratio. Thus a steep rate does not require a direct magnetic-pressure law. We test the full probability model on 394 young TESS rotators with 54 CPVs. A model with one clump and a lognormal spread of closed-loop limits lowers AIC by 4.63 relative to a fitted power law. It lowers total binary log loss by only 1.33 in four withheld groups. With photometric radii the AIC gain is only 0.16. A three-clump model with no closure limit also fits the mean rate. These results do not identify a unique field radius or a material lifetime. The derived law gives tests with inclination and feature count. The bundle includes code, aggregate fits, numerical checks and exact source hashes. External record tables stay in separate scratch.
